Local data contain no H1 2026 statement yet, so the company's 5 August preliminary update is used for newer operating figures. The Scan carries no oneOff or epsStale annotation for RSGN.SW.

6. The case against

The share may be cheap because earnings are already rolling over. H1 adjusted order intake fell 10%, sales fell 13%, EBITDA fell 23%, and FY2026 revenue guidance of CHF410m–CHF420m is roughly flat with FY2025 and below the mid-term growth range. Utility customers have excess inventory and installation bottlenecks, while the higher power-transformer mix takes longer to produce; backlog can look reassuring for years before becoming cash, and factory delays would hurt revenue and margins (H1 update).

The accounting deserves equal scepticism. Much of FY2025's reported growth came from the first full year of Kyte Powertech; CHF180.7m of acquisition goodwill was written directly against equity under Swiss GAAP FER, and the report's theoretical capitalization view shows CHF131.4m residual Kyte goodwill and CHF36.1m of 2025 Kyte goodwill amortisation that did not pass through reported profit (2025 annual report). This is also a short listed history—179 weeks—and a small SIX line where the bid/ask spread and a second commission can matter. The strongest bear case is that the market correctly sees peak transformer margins, acquisition-flattered growth and an expensive capacity build meeting normalized utility demand; the 12.70× multiple is only a gate, not an answer.

NVIDIA's business case is operating performance rather than the screen: FY2023–FY2026 revenue grew eightfold while operating margin rose from 20.7% to 60.4%, and Q2 FY2027 revenue, Data Center revenue and GAAP operating income grew 106%, 117% and 124% respectively (local earnings, Q2 results). Sweep — 30 August 2026

1. Where the world is

Observation. The local market picture is expensive in places but not one-way euphoric. The S&P 500 is 1.3% below its all-time high and up 20.2% over one year, while the Hang Seng is down 0.1% over one year and 2.9% year to date; only 16 of 43 country markets are within 5% of their highs (signals.json, prices.json). US five- and ten-year yields are 19.7% and 10.4% higher than a year ago. WTI is up 27.2% over one year but down 9.5% in three months, while the World Bank's July indices show energy down 1.1% month on month, metals down 2.8%, and European gas up 19.1% (World Bank Commodity Markets). Inference. The shock is easing unevenly, not disappearing. High-duration equities still face a demanding discount rate, and a commodity label is too coarse: exposure to European gas, oil, or industrial metals now means three different things.

Observation. China's July production data split sharply by industry. Industrial value added rose 4.5% year on year and high-tech manufacturing rose 16.9%, but motor-vehicle output fell 0.1%, cement fell 11.6%, and crude processing fell 15.8% (NBS industrial production). January–July industrial profit rose 17.6%; electronics profit rose 110.0% and non-ferrous metals 91.8%, while auto manufacturing profit fell 20.4%. Revenue rose 6.5%, inventories 10.8%, and receivables 8.5% (NBS industrial profits). Inference. This is a selective manufacturing recovery with working-capital accumulation, not a broad industrial boom. It strengthens the case for testing each Chinese holding's cash conversion and end-market position instead of buying the headline growth rate.

Observation. US value retail is winning traffic even while the aggregate consumer signal is mixed. Ross Stores' second-quarter sales rose 13% and comparable sales 10%, primarily from traffic; even excluding a tariff refund, operating margin improved 205 basis points (Ross Stores filing). Walmart US comparable sales excluding fuel rose 2.6%, global e-commerce grew 23%, and US transactions rose 1.5% (Walmart filing). Inference. Consumers are still spending, but value, convenience and treasure-hunt formats are taking share. That supports researching an off-price operator; it does not justify paying any price after a strong release.

2. Leo's reading

All three full-text files in pot/reading/ were read and all three are listed in reading.md; there were no unlisted saved articles. Michael Burry's public archive was also checked because sources.md names him as a useful voice. Its newest item, on Build-A-Bear, is mostly paywalled, so it was used only as a lead and every company fact below comes from the company's own release.

Michael Burry, 26 February — VIEs

The saved article's useful claim remains about sizing, not forecasting: a VIE is an enforceability risk that should change the maximum position, and a non-VIE Hong Kong share is only a relative hedge. Since publication, the locally tracked Hang Seng Tech ETF 3067.HK has fallen 9.2%, Alibaba 19.7%, and BYD 3.2% through 28 August (history.json). The risk is no longer as richly priced, but lower prices do not repair the legal structure. The thesis therefore remains relevant and unproven; the practical consequence is still smaller VIE exposure, not a blanket China call.

Michael Burry, 11 March — common stocks and uncommon value

The Hang Seng Tech ETF is down 8.2% since publication, BYD 6.3%, and Haidilao 26.3% (history.json). PDD's provisional close fell from $102.94 on 11 March to $85.69 on 28 August, down 16.8% (historical price, current price). All three named stocks are cheaper; only price, not thesis quality, improved automatically.

BYD is the material change. At HK$91.95 it remains 23% above the article's HK$75 full-position level (prices.json), while its new interim filing shows first-half revenue down 7.1%, attributable profit down 20.5%, and EPS down 21.1%. Operating cash flow improved to RMB37.3bn, but bills payable rose to RMB53.4bn from RMB22.5bn at year-end (BYD interim filing). That neither confirms nor clears the saved article's supplier-financing concern: cash generation held up, but the bill-financing balance expanded. The operating thesis weakened before the price reached the author's valuation level, so this is a re-look, not an add.

Haidilao's first-half filing still supports a narrower self-help thesis: total revenue rose 7.9%, core operating profit 4.4%, and delivery revenue 121.2%, while core restaurant revenue fell 4.0% and same-store sales 1.3% (HKEX interim filing). It remains on the watchlist from the previous sweep; nothing new today improves yesterday's falsifiers. PDD's second-quarter revenue and operating profit rose 8% while net income fell 12%, but the release still lacks a geography or Pinduoduo/Temu split (PDD release). The disclosure objection survives the lower price, so PDD is again rejected.

Ivan Li, 14 April — convexity

This remains a method article rather than a ticker source. Since publication, local prices put Nvidia up 10.7%, VOO up 10.8%, Amazon up 7.0%, Meta down 12.8%, Netflix down 23.1%, and Tesla down 4.2% (history.json). The dispersion supports the article's point that a few winners can drive long-run returns, but four months cannot establish a multi-decade law. For this pot, patience still ends at a written falsifier, thesis exhaustion, or portfolio-limit breach; there is no mechanical stop and no forced candidate from the article.

3. Candidates

1211.HK — BYD, Hong Kong — re-look, already held

Why: the share is only 6.3% below the saved article date and still above its stated valuation level, while the new filing shows revenue and earnings contracting and bills payable expanding.

What would have to be true: overseas and higher-end growth must offset domestic auto pressure, operating cash conversion must persist without further dependence on supplier financing, and margin deterioration must prove cyclical rather than structural.

BBW — Build-A-Bear Workshop, New York

Why: a fresh Burry lead and a 27 August earnings repricing exposed a contested, simple business: second-quarter revenue fell 7.2% and first-half adjusted pre-tax income fell 18.4%, but it ended the quarter with no revolver borrowings and 674 global locations (company results).

What would have to be true: declining retail and e-commerce demand must stabilise, franchise and commercial growth must represent durable brand monetisation, and earnings power must work without the $7m tariff refund or buyback-supported EPS.

ROST — Ross Stores, Nasdaq

Why: 10% traffic-led comparable sales on top of a 2% prior-year gain, a 205-basis-point underlying margin improvement, and higher store-opening plans suggest share gain rather than mere inflation; the local pipeline can now test whether the post-results price already pays for it.

What would have to be true: new and existing customer traffic must persist through harder comparisons, merchandise availability and markdown discipline must protect the margin gain, and the thesis must remain attractive after removing the tariff refund.

No order, price target or position size is implied. BBW and ROST were added to the watchlist so the normal pipeline can supply prices, history and valuation; 1211.HK was already in the book.

  • China industrial profit mix, inventories and receivables. The National Bureau of Statistics supplied it. Wanted monthly because the auto/electronics split materially changed the BYD read.
  • US consumer traffic and comparable sales by format. Ross Stores and Walmart supplied it. Wanted on results dates because format-level share changes were more informative than the broad spending aggregate.
  • BYD cash conversion and supplier funding. BYD's filing supplied operating cash flow, trade payables and bills payable. Wanted on each filing date because these figures directly test the saved article's concern.
  • Off-universe price and valuation history. Public price pages supplied PDD and Build-A-Bear provisionally; Ross valuation was deliberately left unfilled. This gap is already recorded in the wishlist and should disappear for BBW and ROST after the next normal data fetch.

Local WTI is up 27% over one year but down 10% in three months (signals.json); the IEA says Gulf output was still 8.3m b/d below its pre-war level in July, seaborne product trade was down 3.8m b/d year on year, and Atlantic Basin refining margins reached records (IEA Oil Market Report). 2. Leo's reading

All three full-text files in pot/reading/ were read. Each is listed in reading.md; there were no unlisted saved articles. Michael Burry is the only voice currently named in sources.md, and both of his saved pieces were used as leads, not as sources of company facts.

Power demand is real, but the first-order trade is crowded enough that a good backlog is no longer sufficient.
